description: Package versions that entered the tree inside the 7-day maturity buffer, reviewed 7 and 14 days after publication (advisories, upstream issues, release notes), and dated milestones that ride the same list. Milestones are UTC dates derived from `published`. A review is recorded under `reviews.<milestone>` as { date, outcome: clean | flagged, note }, dated the day it is written and never later; one written up to 2 days before its milestone also carries early: { reason }, and the entry's later milestone stays due. A package entry leaves the list in the change that records its clean 14-day review; a date entry stays, with its `due` review recorded as the evidence that the day was reviewed, or, while what it waits for has not happened, its `due` moves forward with a dated `refs` line naming what was read; a package entry whose version leaves the tree before that review leaves the list too, because nothing is left to review. A date entry marks a contract milestone and never reviews a patched dependency: since 2026-10-15 every patch is watched by scripts/testing/patched-dependencies-gate.mjs, which reads the registry every 6 hours in the patched-dependencies workflow (fitness #48 holds its records), so the date entry patch-storybook-nextjs-vite-10.6.3 that ADR-0037 opened left the list the day the gate landed. A date entry never schedules a dependency move either: since 2026-10-14 (ADR-0036) a non-security bump is taken in the weekly Tuesday window and a toolchain lag is legal for 30 days, so the scheduled hold entries left the list, their evidence in the pull requests that took or retired each move. Read by scripts/testing/maturity-watchlist.mjs (--check in CI, --remind in the maturity-reminder workflow).

entered.via: the root devDependency literal behind pnpm check:duplicates, moved from 5.4.0 with its eight platform binaries about 6.2 days after publication and about 0.8 days before the 2026-10-16T11:42Z maturity, under the owner's 72-hour rule; check:duplicates reads 1003 clones against an unchanged baseline, and a planted clone still exits 1

maturity.note: Reviewed 2026-10-16, the milestone day, about 11 hours after 5.4.1 left the 7-day buffer at 11:42:46Z (published 2026-10-09T11:42:46Z; its eight platform binaries between 11:22:33Z and 11:36:55Z); the reminder opened #626 at 17:10:34Z. Registry, read 2026-10-16T22:38Z: 5.4.1 is latest for jscpd and for each of the eight binaries, and nothing is published after it (the document was last modified at 5.4.1's publication). OSV, at 22:39Z: nothing for jscpd 5.4.1, for any of the eight binaries at 5.4.1, or for jscpd at any version. GitHub: no global advisory affects jscpd, and kucherenko/jscpd lists no repository security advisory. The binary carries four all the same: v5.4.1's rust/Cargo.lock, whose 389 crates.io packages were queried in one OSV batch, pins rustls 0.23.45, inside RUSTSEC-2026-0346 (GHSA-c8m5-c952-6cm4, Debug impls of client session values expose TLS secrets), RUSTSEC-2026-0347 (GHSA-vp88-798v-h67f, buffered application data sent to the outer server after an ECH rejection), RUSTSEC-2026-0348 (GHSA-h2v8-394m-p7vv, Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to 1 GiB before authentication) and RUSTSEC-2026-0349 (GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28, an unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange), all four fixed in 0.23.46; the only other hit is unsafe-libyaml 0.2.11, under RUSTSEC-2024-0449, an unmaintained notice rather than a vulnerability. They are crates.io advisories inside an npm binary, so pnpm audit cannot see them. Upstream moved rustls to 0.23.46 on the default branch on 2026-10-14 (4536dc37, #1201, 'four advisories for rustls 0.23.45') and replaced unsafe-libyaml on 2026-10-12 (cb5ec8d6, #1198); no release carries either yet. Release notes: no release after v5.4.1 (2026-10-09T12:39Z); 5.4.1's own notes carry a hardening fix (#1169): its git subprocesses drop the variables git exports to hooks, a --history range or --baseline-from-ref ref starting with '-' is refused, and an API key an embeddings API echoes in an error is redacted. Upstream issues: five opened in kucherenko/jscpd since 2026-10-09; two name 5.4.1, #1195 (--history fails when log.showSignature is true, closed 2026-10-11 by #1196, unreleased) and #1210 (--semantic counts no JSX element as a call, open), and the other three are feature requests. Reachability: dev-only; one copy, the root devDependency behind pnpm check:duplicates, which no production dependency of the 101 importers reaches. In the Rust build, rustls comes in only through ureq in cpd-semantic (embed/http.rs and embed/models.rs: the embeddings API and the model downloads of --semantic), and unsafe-libyaml through serde_yaml_ng; scripts/testing/jscpd-baseline-gate.mjs runs the token scan with --update-baseline, --baseline and --silent, and .jscpd.json sets no semantic, history or network option, so no rustls advisory is reached here, nor the mode of either issue. Works here: pnpm check:duplicates exits 0 on jscpd 5.4.1 at 2026-10-16T22:40:27Z, 1000 clones in 1799 files, no stale entry and no new clone against the 992-fingerprint baseline, and main be1fa16a's CI run 38976529186 (push, 2026-10-16T22:34Z) passed Duplicate code check (jscpd) at 22:35:05Z. Flagged, not clean: the pinned binary carries four rustls advisories, unreachable here and invisible to pnpm audit, and no jscpd release with rustls 0.23.46 exists yet. The follow-up is the first jscpd release whose rust/Cargo.lock holds rustls 0.23.46 or later, taken in its own PR once mature, 7 days after its publication, with check:duplicates and a planted clone measured on it. The 14-day review is due 2026-10-23.

Registry, read 2026-10-27T00:49Z: 5.4.2 is latest since 2026-10-20T16:14:40Z (GitHub release 16:14:54Z) and matures 2026-10-27T16:14Z; nothing else follows 5.4.1, and the holds gate, run once at 00:55Z, reads jscpd 5.4.1 at or above latest mature.
